Objective: Version2: AW+ 5.4.1 onwards
SFP Copper - 1Gig & Straight Through Cable - Speed/Duplex = Auto & MDIX/MDI mix DUT Port Type: SFP Copper - 1 Gig Partner Port Type: Any Copper - 1 Gig Cable Type: Straight Through Steps:

Note: Not Supported on AR2050V

selections.title: Command Execution: Polarity Bundle polarity mdi polarity auto shutdown polarity mdi polarity auto
selections.justification:
Command Execution: Polarity Bundle polarity mdi polarity auto shutdown polarity mdi polarity auto

[Log-derived analysis] Command-execution resource-usage test for the interface polarity commands (mdi, auto, with an intervening shutdown). With the device in interface-config mode over a bundle of ports, it issues each command, timing execution and measuring the surrounding memory and NSM-message deltas. Reports the measured values and verifies the config is restored to baseline with no exceptions.

step4.objective:
• Automatic MDI/MDI-X resolution on a copper link, with the pair assignment correct for the cable in use — opposite roles at the two ends for a straight-through cable, and the inverse resolution for a crossover cable.
  • Automatic crossover selection in effect as the default, with the resolved MDI or MDI-X role reported per port.
  • Forced MDI and forced MDI-X settings applied and reflected in the operational state, with auto restored afterwards and the port returning to an automatically resolved role.
  • Equivalent automatic crossover resolution over a copper SFP module, including the module-inserted and module-recognised states.
  • Polarity configuration having no effect on media types that do not support it — notably a fibre SFP link — reported as not applicable rather than silently applied, with no change to link state.
  • Invalid or unsupported polarity values rejected with a clear error, the port retaining its prior configuration.
  • Resolved MDI/MDI-X role re-resolving to the same role across an administrative shutdown/no-shutdown cycle and a port reset, with the polarity configuration persisting.

provenance.objective_response:
• A copper link on a fixed (non-SFP) port, cabled with a straight-through cable, is up and stable with speed and duplex resolved by auto-negotiation.
  • Auto-negotiation enabled on both link partners, with the advertised ability sets exchanged and a common highest-capability mode selected.
  • Duplex resolved to full on both ends, with the operational duplex state consistent between local and partner port views.
  • MDI/MDI-X crossover resolved automatically, with the pair assignment correct for a straight-through cable (one end MDI, the other MDI-X).
  • Automatic polarity/crossover selection in effect, with the resolved MDI or MDI-X role reported per port.
  • Equivalent link establishment and duplex/crossover resolution over a 1-Gigabit copper SFP module, including the module-inserted and module-recognised states.
  • Equivalent link establishment over a 1-Gigabit fibre SFP, with MDI/MDI-X configuration having no effect on the fibre media type.
  • Forced (fixed) duplex settings of half and full applied and reflected in the operational state, with auto restored afterwards and the link returning to negotiated full duplex.
  • Forced MDI and MDI-X polarity settings applied and reflected in the operational state, with auto restored afterwards and the link returning to automatically resolved crossover.
  • Link recovery after an administrative shutdown/no-shutdown cycle, with auto-negotiation, duplex and crossover re-resolving to the same end state.
  • Persistence of duplex and polarity configuration across the shutdown/no-shutdown cycle and across a port reset.
  • A duplex mismatch condition (one end forced, the other auto) results in the expected degraded outcome — link up at half duplex or link down — without device instability.
  • Unsupported or invalid duplex and polarity values rejected with a clear error, the port retaining its prior configuration.
  • Duplex and polarity commands rejected or reported as not applicable on media types that do not support them, with no change to link state.
  • Auto-negotiation disabled on one end producing a deterministic, documented link outcome consistent with the fixed settings applied.
  • Bidirectional traffic forwarded without loss or error counter increments while the link is in the negotiated full-duplex state.
  • No late collisions, CRC errors, or FCS errors recorded on a correctly negotiated full-duplex link.
  • Port status output reporting administrative state, operational state, negotiated speed, negotiated duplex, and resolved MDI/MDI-X role.
  • Configuration output reflecting the applied duplex and polarity settings, with defaults omitted or shown as auto as per platform convention.
  • Link up and link down transitions recorded in the system log with accurate port identification and timestamps.
  • Counters and status fields consistent between successive queries and across the link partner's view of the same link.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.

With a straight-through copper cable between the DUT and a link partner, bring the link up with both ends set to auto-negotiation, full duplex and automatic crossover. Confirm the link establishes and check the resolved pair assignment reported at each end for the straight-through cable.

Replace the straight-through cable with a crossover cable on the same copper link, leaving both ends on automatic crossover. Confirm the link re-establishes and compare the resolved role at each end against the result recorded for the straight-through cable.

Confirm automatic crossover is the default polarity setting on a copper port that has never been explicitly configured, and that the port's operational state reports the resolved MDI or MDI-X role rather than only the configured mode.

Force the copper port to MDI, then to MDI-X, allowing the link to settle after each change. Confirm the configured setting is reflected in the port's operational role in each case, and exercise this with the link partner on both a straight-through and a crossover cable so that one combination is a matched pair and one is not.
Return the copper port from a forced setting to automatic crossover. Confirm the port re-resolves its role automatically and no longer reports a forced polarity.

Repeat the automatic crossover resolution over a copper SFP module on a port that accepts pluggables, using a straight-through cable to a partner. Confirm the module is detected and recognised as a copper transceiver, the link comes up, and a resolved MDI or MDI-X role is reported for the SFP port.

Apply polarity configuration to a port carrying a fibre SFP link. Confirm the DUT reports the setting as not applicable to the media type rather than accepting it silently, and check the link state before and after the attempt.

Attempt to set polarity to values outside the supported set, including a malformed or unsupported keyword, on a copper port with a known good configuration. Confirm each attempt is rejected with an error and that the port's prior polarity configuration and link state are unchanged.

On a copper link with an automatically resolved role, record the resolved role, then administratively shut down and re-enable the port. Confirm the link re-establishes, the role resolves to the same value, and the polarity configuration is unchanged.

Repeat the disruption test with a forced polarity setting in place and across a port reset rather than an administrative cycle. Confirm the configured polarity persists across the reset and the operational role returns to the configured value once the link is up.

Exercise polarity changes in combination with duplex changes on the same copper port — alternating between forced and automatic settings for each in turn, including a shutdown between changes. Confirm each command is accepted in sequence and that the port's reported duplex and polarity state remain consistent with the last applied configuration.

  • Automatic crossover selection in effect as the default, with the resolved MDI or MDI-X role reported per port.
  • Forced MDI and forced MDI-X settings applied and reflected in the operational state, with auto restored afterwards and the port returning to an automatically resolved role.
  • Equivalent automatic crossover resolution over a copper SFP module, including the module-inserted and module-recognised states.
  • Polarity configuration having no effect on media types that do not support it — notably a fibre SFP link — reported as not applicable rather than silently applied, with no change to link state.
  • Invalid or unsupported polarity values rejected with a clear error, the port retaining its prior configuration.
  • Resolved MDI/MDI-X role re-resolving to the same role across an administrative shutdown/no-shutdown cycle and a port reset, with the polarity configuration persisting.

gaps: The selected ART coverage (1342.301.13 and 1342.301.14) exercises the command-execution surface for polarity and duplex settings, including the mdi/auto and half/auto bundles across shutdown transitions, so CLI acceptance, persistence of configured values, and basic interface-state handling for these attributes are reasonably addressed. What remains uncovered is the negotiated outcome itself: the manual case (AWP-12285) depends on a live link between a DUT configured for Auto speed, Full duplex and MDI polarity and a partner set to MDIX, with EEE/low-power-idle enabled on both ends, and the automation does not establish or observe that paired-endpoint result — link establishment, resolved speed/duplex/polarity after negotiation, and cable-type (straight) sensitivity are all outside its scope. Media-specific behaviour is likewise absent, notably the expected rejection of polarity configuration on SFP ports and the fibre/copper SFP variants implied by AWP-104 and AWPTCM-T13268. Observability of the negotiated and EEE-active state on both devices, rather than the configuration command alone, is the principal gap, so the manual case retains value for cross-device interoperability and media-dependent error handling.
